55	def write_report(payload: dict[str, object], exit_code: int) -> int:
56	    REPORT_PATH.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
57	    text = json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
58	    REPORT_PATH.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
59	    print(text, end="")

62	
63	def max_bond_error(framework) -> float:
64	    graph = framework.graph
65	    cell = np.asarray(graph.graph["cell"], dtype=float)
66	    inverse = np.linalg.inv(cell)
67	    errors: list[float] = []
68	
69	    def target_bond_length(left: int, right: int) -> float:
70	        left_symbol = graph.nodes[left]["symbol"]
71	        right_symbol = graph.nodes[right]["symbol"]
72	        return float(CovalentRadius.radius[left_symbol] + CovalentRadius.radius[right_symbol])
73	
74	    for left, right in graph.edges():
75	        if graph.nodes[left]["slot"] == graph.nodes[right]["slot"]:
76	            continue
77	        delta = np.asarray(graph.nodes[left]["coord"], dtype=float) - np.asarray(
78	            graph.nodes[right]["coord"], dtype=float
79	        )
80	        delta -= np.round(delta @ inverse) @ cell
81	        errors.append(abs(float(np.linalg.norm(delta)) - target_bond_length(left, right)))
82	    if not errors:
83	        raise ValueError("no inter-slot bonds were found in the public case")
84	    return max(errors)

87	def build_public_case(topology_name: str) -> tuple[object, object, float, float]:
88	    sys.path.insert(0, str(SOURCE_ROOT / "src"))
89	    from autografs import Autografs
90	
91	    mofgen = Autografs()
92	    topology = mofgen.topologies[topology_name]
93	    building_units = mofgen.list_building_units(sieve=topology_name)
94	    mappings = {slot_type: options[0] for slot_type, options in building_units.items()}
95	
96	    baseline = mofgen.build(topology, mappings=dict(mappings), max_rmsd=1.0)
97	    relaxed = mofgen.build(
98	        topology,
99	        mappings=dict(mappings),
100	        max_rmsd=1.0,
101	        relax_embedding=True,
102	    )
103	    return baseline, relaxed, max_bond_error(baseline), max_bond_error(relaxed)

106	def main() -> int:
107	    try:
108	        observations: list[dict[str, object]] = []
109	        for case in CASES:

111	                case["topology_name"]
112	            )
113	            baseline_volume = float(baseline.structure.volume)
114	            relaxed_volume = float(relaxed.structure.volume)
115	            error_delta = relaxed_error - baseline_error
116	            volume_delta = relaxed_volume - baseline_volume
117	
118	            if not all(
119	                math.isfinite(value)

121	                    baseline_error,
122	                    relaxed_error,
123	                    baseline_volume,
124	                    relaxed_volume,
125	                    error_delta,
126	                    volume_delta,
127	                ]

131	                )

135	                "role": case["role"],
136	                "topology_name": case["topology_name"],
137	                "baseline_max_bond_error": baseline_error,
138	                "relaxed_max_bond_error": relaxed_error,
139	                "bond_error_delta": error_delta,
140	                "closure_budget": CLOSURE_BUDGET,
141	                "within_budget": relaxed_error <= baseline_error + CLOSURE_BUDGET,
142	                "budget_margin": baseline_error + CLOSURE_BUDGET - relaxed_error,
143	                "baseline_volume": baseline_volume,
144	                "relaxed_volume": relaxed_volume,
145	                "volume_delta": volume_delta,

147	                "volume_ratio_limit": CELL_VOLUME_RATIO_LIMIT,
148	                "within_volume_budget": relaxed_volume

157	                    and np.allclose(

159	                        relaxed.structure.cart_coords,
160	                    )
161	                )
162	            observations.append(record)

164	        lower_symmetry_ok = all(
165	            bool(record["within_budget"] and record["within_volume_budget"])
166	            for record in observations
167	            if record["role"] == "lower_symmetry"
168	        )
169	        pinned_control = next(
170	            record for record in observations if record["role"] == "pinned_control"
171	        )
172	        pinned_ok = bool(pinned_control["structure_unchanged"])
173	
174	        return write_report(
175	            {
176	                "schema_version": "1.0",
177	                "status": "post_fix_success" if lower_symmetry_ok and pinned_ok else "pre_fix_expected_failure",
178	                "observation": {

1	# AuToGraFS calibrated relaxed embedding
2	
3	AuToGraFS generates framework structures from topological blueprints and
4	building units. The relevant behavior for this task is the optional relaxed
5	embedding workflow, which allows slot positions to move during optimization
6	while preserving the assigned net.
7	
8	The supplied public panel shows that this path can produce geometry that is
9	inconsistent with the ordinary build on several valid lower-symmetry inputs,
10	while a pinned control remains unchanged. The relaxed workflow is not required
11	to beat the ordinary build in every case, but it must stay within the
12	documented closure and volume envelopes.
13	
14	## What the public reproduction checks
15

17	panel of valid inputs and reports the measured geometry.

20

24	  optimize.

26	  budgets on the supplied lower-symmetry cases.

28	  consistent across the supplied panel.

1	# Building frameworks (Python API)
2	
3	*Part of the [AuToGraFS documentation](../README.md#documentation).*
4	
5	For the mechanics behind these calls — the sieve, alignment, and cell
6	optimization — see [How it works](internals.md).
7	
8	## Exploring the libraries
9	
10	```python
11	from autografs import Autografs
12	
13	mofgen = Autografs()
14	
15	mofgen.list_topologies()                        # all RCSR symbols
16	mofgen.list_topologies(sieve="Benzene_linear")  # nets this SBU fits
17	
18	# building units compatible with a net, grouped by slot type;
19	# slot types with no compatible SBU are absent from the dict
20	mofgen.list_building_units(sieve="srs")
21	
22	# raw access
23	sbu = mofgen.sbu["Zn_mof5_octahedral"]          # a Fragment
24	topology = mofgen.topologies["tbo"]             # a Topology (lazy library)
25	zeolite = mofgen.topologies["FAU"]              # IZA framework codes work too
26	
27	print(len(topology))                  # number of slots
28	print(topology.cell.abc)              # blueprint cell
29	print(topology.spacegroup_number)     # 225
30	print(topology.is_2d)                 # False
31	for slot_type, indices in topology.mappings.items():
32	    print(slot_type, "fills slots", indices)
33	```
34	
35	55 IZA zeolite framework type codes (FAU, LTA, CHA, SOD, RHO, ...) resolve
36	as lookup-only aliases onto the RCSR nets that carry them in lowercase —
37	`mofgen.topologies["FAU"]` and `mofgen.topologies["fau"]` are the same
38	entry, and enumeration (`build_all`, coverage counts) never sees a net
39	twice. The mapping ships in `data/iza_aliases.json` (regenerate with
40	`scripts/make_iza_aliases.py`); `mofgen.topologies.aliases` lists it.
41	
42	## Building
43	
44	`build` takes a topology and a mapping from slot types (or explicit slot
45	indices) to SBUs, given as library names or `Fragment` objects:
46	
47	```python
48	mof = mofgen.build(
49	    topology,
50	    mappings={node_type: "Zn_mof5_octahedral", edge_type: "Benzene_linear"},
51	    refine_cell=True,   # optimize cell parameters (default)
52	    max_rmsd=0.3,       # reject builds with bad shape matches
53	    min_distance=1.0,   # reject builds with overlapping atoms
54	)
55	```
56	
57	- **`max_rmsd`** gates the *directional* mismatch between an SBU's connection
58	  vectors and its slot's (dimensionless; 0 is a perfect shape match).
59	  Incompatible geometry raises `autografs.AlignmentError` instead of returning
60	  a distorted structure.
61	- **`min_distance`** screens the built structure: if any two non-bonded atoms
62	  (all periodic images included) are closer than this many Å,
63	  `autografs.OverlapError` is raised instead of returning overlapping or
64	  interpenetrating output. The same check is available on any result as
65	  `Framework.min_contact()`.
66	- **Slot indices** (integers) may be used as mapping keys to place a specific
67	  SBU on a specific slot, overriding the slot-type choice:
68	
69	```python
70	mappings = {node_type: "sbu_A", edge_type: "linker_1", 7: "linker_2"}
71	```
72	
73	### Embedding relaxation
74	
75	A build normally places every SBU at its blueprint slot centre and varies only
76	the cell's free parameters, so the *proportions* of the structure are whatever
77	the net's idealized (maximum-symmetry, near-equal-edge) embedding chose. For
78	high-symmetry nets those are exact by symmetry — pcu, dia, fcu and friends
79	have nothing to choose — but lower-symmetry nets inherit proportions that can
80	be measurably wrong for real chemistry: no single cell parameter can give a
81	long linker and a short one each the room they need.
82	
83	```python
84	mof = mofgen.build(topology, mappings, relax_embedding=True)
85	```
86	
87	frees the slot centres as extra optimization degrees of freedom while
88	preserving the declared symmetry of the net. Fully pinned nets (their
89	embedding is already exact by symmetry) have nothing to relax and build
90	exactly as without the flag; for the rest, the topology of the output is
91	unchanged (`verify_net` applies as usual) while the packing follows the SBUs
92	instead of the idealization. Off by default; the geometry of default builds
93	is unchanged.
94	
95	## Batch enumeration
96	
97	`build_all` attempts every compatible SBU combination on every (or a subset
98	of) topology:
99	
100	```python
101	frameworks = mofgen.build_all(
102	    topology_subset=["pcu", "dia", "srs"],
103	    sbu_subset=None,          # default: whole SBU library
104	    max_rmsd=0.3,
105	    min_distance=1.0,
106	    max_per_topology=50,      # cap the combinatorial explosion...
107	    seed=42,                  # ...with a reproducible random sample
108	    n_jobs=4,                 # parallel builds (near-linear speedup)
109	)
110	```
111	
112	Failed builds are counted and skipped, not raised. Multinodal nets have
113	combinatorially many SBU choices; when the full product exceeds
114	`max_per_topology`, a seeded sample of distinct combinations is built instead.
115	Passing `max_per_topology=-1` (or `None`, the default) disables the cap and
116	enumerates exhaustively. Either way the total combination count over all
117	buildable topologies is logged before the first build starts, so an
118	exhaustive run can be cost-estimated — and aborted — while still cheap.
119	
120	Long runs can checkpoint: with `checkpoint_dir="ckpt/"` every finished
121	combination is recorded on disk atomically (built frameworks as `.json.gz`,
122	gate rejections as `.failed` markers), and rerunning with the same arguments
123	and the same directory skips them, reloading their outcomes instead of
124	rebuilding — an interrupted enumeration resumes where it stopped. The ledger
125	records outcomes, not settings, so rerun with the same gates and seed.
126	
127	## Working with the result
128	
129	`build` returns a `Framework`:
130	
131	```python
132	mof.structure          # pymatgen Structure (wrapped; site props: tags, ufftype)
133	mof.graph              # networkx bond graph: symbols, coords, UFF4MOF
134	                       # atom types, bond orders, tags (source of truth)
135	mof.formula            # 'Zn4 H12 C24 O13'
136	mof.lattice            # pymatgen Lattice
137	mof.bonds              # [(i, j, bond_order), ...]
138	mof.mmtypes            # UFF4MOF atom types, node order
139	mof.min_contact()      # closest non-bonded contact (all images)
140	mof.slots              # {slot index: SBU name} for every placed unit
141	
142	mof.density                     # g/cm3 (MOF-5: ~0.6)
143	mof.void_fraction()             # geometric; probe_radius=1.2 for a He probe
144	mof.largest_cavity_diameter()   # LCD, Angstrom (MOF-5: ~15)
145	mof.pore_limiting_diameter()    # PLD, Angstrom (MOF-5: ~8) - the channel bottleneck
146	
147	mof.write_cif("out.cif", symprec=None)   # symprec symmetrizes if set
148	atoms = mof.to_ase()                     # periodic ase.Atoms
149	mof.view()                               # ASE viewer
150	gulp_input = mof.to_gulp()               # UFF4MOF optimization input for GULP
151	```
152	
153	CIF export is for downstream tools; it loses the bond graph and the
154	per-atom provenance that post-build editing needs. To keep a framework
155	editable across sessions, save it to the versioned JSON format instead:
156	
157	```python
158	mof.save("mof5.json.gz")                 # bond graph, tags, provenance, energy
159	mof = Framework.load("mof5.json.gz")     # editable exactly like the original
160	defective = mof.supercell(2).defects(fraction=0.1, seed=42)
161	```
162	
163	See [Editing](editing.md) for supercells, defects, and functionalization.
164	
165	## UFF4MOF relaxation
166	
167	`relax` optimizes the geometry and cell with the UFF4MOF force field through
168	LAMMPS, in-process, and returns a new `Framework` with the same bond graph:
169	
170	```bash
171	pip install "autografs[relax]"
172	```
173	
174	```python
175	relaxed = mof.relax()          # UFF4MOF, alternating cell + FIRE
176	relaxed.energy                 # kcal/mol per unit cell
177	relaxed.write_cif("relaxed.cif")
178	```
179	
180	Cells smaller than the non-bonded cutoff (12.5 Å by default) are relaxed as an
181	internal supercell and folded back transparently. `"UFF"` and `"Dreiding"` are
182	also accepted as `force_field`.
183	
184	### Higher levels: any ASE calculator
185	
186	Passing `calculator` switches `relax` to a thin ASE bridge — the higher rungs
187	of a multi-fidelity funnel. Use a name or any ASE calculator instance:
188	
189	```python
190	relaxed = mof.relax(calculator="gfn-ff")   # periodic GFN-FF (xtb-python)
191	relaxed = mof.relax(calculator="gfn1")     # GFN1-xTB (pip install tblite)
192	relaxed = mof.relax(calculator="dftb")     # DFTB+ (binary + SK files)
193	relaxed = mof.relax(calculator=my_ase_calculator, fmax=0.01, steps=1000)
194	```
195	
196	The bond graph is preserved exactly as on the LAMMPS path, energies land in
197	`Framework.energy` in the same kcal/mol-per-cell convention, and
198	`relax_cell=False` keeps the cell fixed (cell relaxation needs a calculator
199	that provides stress). `"gfn2"` is rejected up front: GFN2-xTB has no
200	periodic implementation.
201	
202	## Partial charges
203	
204	`assign_charges` puts per-atom point charges on the bond graph — the input
205	GCMC adsorption codes need. The built-in scheme is EQeq (extended charge
206	equilibration, Wilmer et al. 2012): periodic, parameter-free beyond two
207	published dials, no DFT required, one linear solve. The implementation is a
208	numpy port validated against the reference C++ code:
209	
210	```python
211	charged = mof.assign_charges("eqeq")   # returns a new Framework
212	charged.charges                        # per-atom array, sums to 0
213	charged.write_cif("charged.cif")       # gains _atom_site_charge (RASPA-style)
214	charged.to_ase()                       # charges become ASE initial charges
215	charged.save("charged.json.gz")        # charges survive save/load and editing
216	```
217	
218	Other schemes (DDEC from DFT output, ML charge models) plug in through a
219	registry:
220	
221	```python
222	from autografs.charges import register_charge_method
223	
224	@register_charge_method("mymodel")
225	def my_charges(framework, **options):
226	    return model.predict(framework)    # one charge per atom, node order
227	
228	charged = mof.assign_charges("mymodel")
229	```
230	
231	Treat the scheme as a controlled variable in any adsorption study — EQeq and
232	DDEC charges differ systematically, and uptake predictions inherit that
233	difference.
234	
235	## Elastic constants
236	
237	`elastic_properties` computes the 6×6 stiffness tensor at the same force-field
238	level (same optional install), by central finite differences of the LAMMPS
239	stress under the six Voigt strains after a full relaxation — the protocol of
240	the LAMMPS `ELASTIC` example, run in-process:
241	
242	```python

244	props.stiffness                    # 6x6 Voigt matrix, GPa, symmetrized

252	The tensor is projected onto the framework's crystal system (averaged over its
253	point-group rotations), so a cubic framework reports the exact 3-constant
254	cubic pattern. Note that the detected symmetry is that of the *built model*,

257	through ring disorder). Treat the numbers as screening-level: UFF4MOF
258	stiffnesses carry force-field error; rankings across candidates are the
259	reliable output. For 2D layer frameworks only the in-plane components are
260	physical — the padded c axis is not.
261	
262	## Error handling
263	
264	All library exceptions derive from `autografs.AutografsError`:
265

272	except AlignmentError:   # shape mismatch beyond the gate
273	    ...
274	except OverlapError:     # non-bonded contact below the gate

409	    @property
410	    def n_slot_free(self) -> int:
411	        return 0 if self.slot_disp is None else self.slot_disp.n_free
412	
413	    def split(self, params: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
414	        """Cell block and slot block of the packed parameter vector."""
415	        params = np.asarray(params, dtype=float)
416	        n_cell = self.cell_param.n_free
417	        return params[:n_cell], params[n_cell:]
418	
419	    def _shifts(self, slot_free: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray | None:
420	        """Per-topology-slot fractional displacements, or None.
421	
422	        None also for a relaxation-enabled plan on a fully pinned
423	        blueprint: with no displacement to select between, the
424	        augmented objective has nothing useful to steer, so the legacy
425	        objective is retained.
426	        """
427	        if self.slot_disp is None or self.slot_disp.n_free == 0:
428	            return None
429	        return self.slot_disp.expand(slot_free)
430	
431	    @functools.cached_property
432	    def _blueprint_matrix(self) -> np.ndarray:
433	        a, b, c = self.blueprint_abc
434	        return Lattice.from_parameters(a, b, c, *self.angles).matrix
435	
436	    def matrix_for(self, free: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
437	        return Lattice.from_parameters(*self.cell_param.expand(free)).matrix
438	
439	    def initial_parameters(self) -> np.ndarray:
440	        """Analytic starting parameters from bond-through distances.
441	
442	        Each anchor pair wants its two slot centers separated by the
443	        center-to-anchor spans plus the bond length; the blueprint
444	        separation scales with the cell, so the ratio of sums is a
445	        near-optimal isotropic starting scale (exact for uninodal
446	        cubic nets). The resulting (a, b, c) guess is reduced to the
447	        crystal system's free parameters.
448	        """
449	        blueprint = self._blueprint_matrix
450	        required = 0.0
451	        current = 0.0
452	        for index_a, target_a, index_b, target_b, offset in self.pairs:
453	            pa = self.placements[index_a]
454	            pb = self.placements[index_b]
455	            span_a = np.linalg.norm(pa.anchor_vecs[pa.arm_for_target[target_a]])
456	            span_b = np.linalg.norm(pb.anchor_vecs[pb.arm_for_target[target_b]])
457	            required += (
458	                float(span_a)
459	                + float(span_b)
460	                + self._pair_bond_length(index_a, target_a, index_b, target_b)
461	            )
462	            separation = (pa.frac_center - pb.frac_center - offset) @ blueprint
463	            current += float(np.linalg.norm(separation))
464	        if not self.pairs or current < 1e-9:
465	            # no shared dummies: fall back to matching mean arm lengths
466	            arms = np.concatenate([p.arm_lengths for p in self.placements]).mean()
467	            slot_arms = np.concatenate(
468	                [
469	                    np.linalg.norm(p.frac_arms @ blueprint, axis=1)
470	                    for p in self.placements
471	                ]
472	            ).mean()
473	            abc_guess = self.blueprint_abc * (arms / slot_arms)
474	        else:
475	            abc_guess = self.blueprint_abc * (required / current)
476	        seed = self.cell_param.seed(abc_guess)
477	        # slot displacements start at the idealized embedding
478	        return np.concatenate([seed, np.zeros(self.n_slot_free)])
479	
480	    def _pair_bond_length(
481	        self, index_a: int, target_a: int, index_b: int, target_b: int
482	    ) -> float:
483	        """Target bond length between a pair's two anchors."""
484	        pa = self.placements[index_a]
485	        pb = self.placements[index_b]
486	        return float(
487	            pa.anchor_radii[pa.arm_for_target[target_a]]
488	            + pb.anchor_radii[pb.arm_for_target[target_b]]
489	        )
490	
491	    def residual(self, params: np.ndarray) -> float:
492	        """RMS objective at these parameters, in Angstrom.
493	
494	        Both the fixed and relaxed paths score pairwise anchor geometry
495	        with the same distance-based residual. When slot displacements
496	        are active, the displaced coordinates are folded into that same
497	        measure.
498	        """
499	        cell_free, slot_free = self.split(params)
500	        matrix = self.matrix_for(cell_free)
501	        shifts = self._shifts(slot_free)
502	        if shifts is None:
503	            positions = [p.anchor_positions(matrix) for p in self.placements]
504	            total = 0.0
505	            for index_a, target_a, index_b, target_b, offset in self.pairs:
506	                delta = (
507	                    positions[index_a][target_a]
508	                    - positions[index_b][target_b]
509	                    - offset @ matrix
510	                )
511	                gap = float(np.sqrt(delta @ delta)) - self._pair_bond_length(
512	                    index_a, target_a, index_b, target_b
513	                )
514	                total += gap * gap
515	            return float(np.sqrt(total / len(self.pairs)))
516	        geometries = [
517	            p.placed_geometry(matrix, shifts[p.slot_index]) for p in self.placements
518	        ]
519	        total = 0.0
520	        for index_a, target_a, index_b, target_b, offset in self.pairs:
521	            anchors_a, directions_a = geometries[index_a]
522	            anchors_b, directions_b = geometries[index_b]
523	            # Bond vector from anchor a to anchor b's paired image.
524	            bond = anchors_b[target_b] + offset @ matrix - anchors_a[target_a]
525	            length = float(np.sqrt(bond @ bond))
526	            target = self._pair_bond_length(index_a, target_a, index_b, target_b)
527	            gap = length - target
528	            # Directional deviation at both ends.
529	            miss_a = bond - length * directions_a[target_a]
530	            miss_b = -bond - length * directions_b[target_b]
531	            total += gap * gap + float(miss_a @ miss_a) + float(miss_b @ miss_b)
532	        return float(np.sqrt(total / (3 * len(self.pairs))))
533	
534	    def finalize(
535	        self, params: np.ndarray
536	    ) -> tuple[list[Fragment], Lattice, dict[int, float]]:
537	        """Place every SBU rigidly in the final cell.
538	
539	        Re-solves the full direction match (assignment included) at the
540	        final cell, then maps each SBU's atoms with the resulting rigid
541	        rotation + translation. Atoms keep their internal geometry;
542	        dummies receive the tags of their assigned slot dummies so the
543	        graph builder can bond paired fragments. Slot displacements
544	        (when active) shift each SBU's centre; the unit stays rigid.
545	
546	        Returns
547	        -------
548	        tuple[list[Fragment], Lattice, dict[int, float]]
549	            Aligned fragments, the final lattice, and the per-slot
550	            directional RMSD (dimensionless shape mismatch).
551	        """
552	        cell_free, slot_free = self.split(params)
553	        lattice = Lattice.from_parameters(*self.cell_param.expand(cell_free))
554	        matrix = lattice.matrix
555	        shifts = self._shifts(slot_free)
556	        fragments: list[Fragment] = []
557	        slot_rmsds: dict[int, float] = {}
558	        for placement in self.placements:
559	            directions = _unit(placement.frac_arms @ matrix)
560	            rotation, perm, rmsd = match_directions(directions, placement.arm_units)
561	            placement.arm_for_target = perm
562	            slot_rmsds[placement.slot_index] = rmsd
563	            frac_center = placement.frac_center
564	            if shifts is not None:
565	                frac_center = frac_center + shifts[placement.slot_index]
566	            center = frac_center @ matrix
567	            sbu = placement.sbu
568	            coords = (
569	                sbu.atoms.cart_coords - placement.sbu_center
570	            ) @ rotation.T + center
571	            tags = [0] * len(sbu.atoms)
572	            for target_index, arm_index in enumerate(perm):
573	                atom_index = placement.dummy_indices[arm_index]
574	                tags[atom_index] = placement.tags[target_index]
575	            aligned = Molecule(
576	                sbu.atoms.species, coords, site_properties={"tags": tags}
577	            )
578	            fragments.append(
579	                Fragment(
580	                    atoms=aligned,
581	                    name=sbu.name,
582	                    pointgroup=sbu.pointgroup,
583	                )
584	            )
585	        return fragments, lattice, slot_rmsds
586	
587	
588	def _find_anchors(
589	    sbu: Fragment, dummy_indices: list[int], center: np.ndarray
590	) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
591	    """Anchor vectors (relative to center) and covalent radii per arm.
592	
593	    The anchor of an arm is the real atom bonded through it - the
594	    dummy's nearest non-dummy atom; the built structure bonds paired
595	    anchors together, so the cell objective targets one covalent bond
596	    length between them. A fragment with no real atoms (synthetic test
597	    fixtures) falls back to the dummies themselves with zero radius,
598	    which turns the pair objective back into dummy coincidence.
599	    """
600	    coords = np.asarray(sbu.atoms.cart_coords)
601	    real = [i for i, site in enumerate(sbu.atoms) if site.specie.symbol != "X"]
602	    if not real:
603	        return coords[dummy_indices] - center, np.zeros(len(dummy_indices))
604	    vecs = np.empty((len(dummy_indices), 3))
605	    radii = np.empty(len(dummy_indices))
606	    for k, dummy in enumerate(dummy_indices):
607	        distances = np.linalg.norm(coords[real] - coords[dummy], axis=1)
608	        nearest = real[int(np.argmin(distances))]
609	        vecs[k] = coords[nearest] - center
610	        symbol = sbu.atoms[nearest].specie.symbol
611	        # an element missing from the Cordero table keeps the library's
612	        # half-bond convention: the dummy sits half a bond from its anchor
613	        radii[k] = CovalentRadius.radius.get(symbol, float(distances.min()))
614	    return vecs, radii
615	
616	
617	def prepare_build(
618	    topology: Topology,
619	    mappings: dict[int, Fragment],
620	    relax_embedding: bool = False,
621	) -> BuildPlan:
622	    """Precompute all geometry for building one framework.
623	
624	    Parameters
625	    ----------
626	    topology : Topology
627	        The blueprint; not modified.
628	    mappings : dict[int, Fragment]
629	        Slot index to (private) SBU fragment, as produced by
630	        Autografs._validate_mappings.
631	    relax_embedding : bool, optional
632	        Add the blueprint's slot displacements as optimizer degrees of
633	        freedom (see autografs.symmetry). Fully pinned nets (pcu and
634	        most high-symmetry blueprints) have nothing to relax and keep
635	        the legacy objective exactly.
636	
637	    Returns
638	    -------
639	    BuildPlan
640	        Arrays and the shared-dummy pair table for the optimizer.
641	
642	    Raises
643	    ------
644	    AlignmentError
645	        If an SBU's dummy count does not match its slot's.
646	    """
647	    blueprint = topology.cell
648	    placements: list[SlotPlacement] = []
649	    # tag -> list of (placement index, target index, fractional position)
650	    tag_sites: dict[int, list[tuple[int, int, np.ndarray]]] = {}
651	    for slot_index, sbu in sorted(mappings.items()):
652	        slot = topology.slots[slot_index]
653	        dummy_idx = [
654	            i for i, site in enumerate(slot.atoms) if site.specie.symbol == "X"
655	        ]
656	        slot_frac = blueprint.get_fractional_coords(slot.atoms.cart_coords[dummy_idx])
657	        frac_center = slot_frac.mean(axis=0)
658	        slot_tags = [int(slot.atoms[i].properties["tags"]) for i in dummy_idx]
659	
660	        sbu_dummy_idx = [
661	            i for i, site in enumerate(sbu.atoms) if site.specie.symbol == "X"
662	        ]
663	        if len(sbu_dummy_idx) != len(dummy_idx):
664	            raise AlignmentError(
665	                f"SBU {sbu.name!r} has {len(sbu_dummy_idx)} connection "
666	                f"points but slot {slot_index} of {topology.name!r} "
667	                f"needs {len(dummy_idx)}."
668	            )
669	        sbu_dummies = sbu.atoms.cart_coords[sbu_dummy_idx]
670	        sbu_center = sbu_dummies.mean(axis=0)
671	        arm_vectors = sbu_dummies - sbu_center
672	        arm_lengths = np.linalg.norm(arm_vectors, axis=1)
673	        arm_units = _unit(arm_vectors)
674	        anchor_vecs, anchor_radii = _find_anchors(sbu, sbu_dummy_idx, sbu_center)
675	        # anchor -> dummy: the bond direction the SBU wants; dummy-only
676	        # fixtures (anchor == dummy) fall back to the centroid arm
677	        bond_vectors = arm_vectors - anchor_vecs
678	        bond_norms = np.linalg.norm(bond_vectors, axis=1, keepdims=True)
679	        degenerate = bond_norms[:, 0] < 1e-6
680	        bond_units = np.where(
681	            degenerate[:, None], arm_units, bond_vectors / np.maximum(bond_norms, 1e-12)
682	        )
683	
684	        frac_arms = slot_frac - frac_center
685	        # reference assignment at the blueprint cell
686	        directions = _unit(frac_arms @ blueprint.matrix)
687	        _, perm, _ = match_directions(directions, arm_units)
688	        placement = SlotPlacement(
689	            slot_index=slot_index,
690	            frac_center=frac_center,
691	            frac_arms=frac_arms,
692	            tags=slot_tags,
693	            sbu=sbu,
694	            arm_units=arm_units,
695	            arm_lengths=arm_lengths,
696	            sbu_center=sbu_center,
697	            dummy_indices=sbu_dummy_idx,
698	            anchor_vecs=anchor_vecs,
699	            anchor_radii=anchor_radii,
700	            bond_units=bond_units,
701	            arm_for_target=perm,
702	        )
703	        index = len(placements)
704	        placements.append(placement)
705	        for target_index, (tag, frac) in enumerate(
706	            zip(slot_tags, slot_frac, strict=True)
707	        ):
708	            tag_sites.setdefault(tag, []).append((index, target_index, frac))
709	
710	    pairs: list[tuple[int, int, int, int, np.ndarray]] = []
711	    unpaired = 0
712	    for tag, entries in sorted(tag_sites.items()):
713	        if len(entries) == 1:
714	            unpaired += 1
715	            continue
716	        if len(entries) > 2:
717	            logger.warning(
718	                f"Tag {tag} shared by {len(entries)} slots; using the first two."
719	            )
720	        (index_a, target_a, frac_a), (index_b, target_b, frac_b) = entries[:2]
721	        offset = np.round(frac_a - frac_b)
722	        pairs.append((index_a, target_a, index_b, target_b, offset))
723	    if unpaired:
724	        logger.debug(
725	            f"{unpaired} dummies are not shared between slots; they do "
726	            "not constrain the cell."
727	        )
728	    abc = np.array(blueprint.abc, dtype=float)
729	    angles = (
730	        float(blueprint.angles[0]),
731	        float(blueprint.angles[1]),
732	        float(blueprint.angles[2]),
733	    )
734	    cell_param = CellParametrization(
735	        spacegroup_number=getattr(topology, "spacegroup_number", None),
736	        blueprint_abc=(float(abc[0]), float(abc[1]), float(abc[2])),
737	        blueprint_angles=angles,
738	        is_2d=getattr(topology, "is_2d", False),
739	    )
740	    slot_disp = None
741	    if relax_embedding:
742	        from autografs.symmetry import orbit_displacements
743	
744	        slot_disp = orbit_displacements(topology)
745	        if slot_disp.n_free:
746	            logger.debug(
747	                f"Embedding relaxation on {topology.name!r}: "
748	                f"{slot_disp.n_free} slot parameters over "
749	                f"{len(slot_disp.bases)} orbits."
750	            )
751	    return BuildPlan(
752	        placements=placements,
753	        pairs=pairs,
754	        blueprint_abc=abc,
755	        angles=angles,
756	        cell_param=cell_param,
757	        slot_disp=slot_disp,
758	    )

1	"""
2	Blueprint symmetry operations, derived from the blueprint itself.
3	
4	The embedding-relaxation mode needs to displace slot centres
5	without breaking the net's declared symmetry: one displacement per
6	crystallographic orbit, restricted to the directions the site's
7	stabilizer allows, and propagated to the orbit's other slots by the
8	operations relating them. That needs the space-group *operations*, and
9	``Topology`` only records the spacegroup *number* - recovering
10	operations from the number alone would reintroduce a setting/origin
11	ambiguity against whatever convention the CGD idealization chose.
12	
13	This module derives the operations numerically from the slot-centre
14	set instead, so they agree with the stored embedding by construction:
15	
16	1. candidate rotation parts are the integer matrices preserving the
17	   cell's metric tensor (the lattice's point group, proper and
18	   improper - mirrors constrain displacements too);
19	2. each rotation is kept with every translation that maps the
20	   slot-centre set onto itself while preserving orbit labels;
21	3. a site's allowed displacement subspace is the common fixed space of
22	   its stabilizer's rotation parts;
23	4. an orbit representative's displacement propagates to each member
24	   through (the rotation part of) one operation mapping the
25	   representative onto it.
26	
27	Everything is exact in the tolerance of the stored coordinates; the
28	identity operation always survives, so the machinery degrades to
29	"every orbit fully free" for a P1 blueprint rather than failing.
30	"""
31	
32	from __future__ import annotations
33	
34	import logging
35	from dataclasses import dataclass
36	from itertools import product
37	
38	import numpy as np
39	
40	from autografs.topology import Topology
41	
42	__all__ = [
43	    "SymmetryOperation",
44	    "OrbitDisplacements",
45	    "blueprint_operations",
46	    "orbit_displacements",
47	]
48	
49	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
50	
51	# fractional-coordinate agreement for "the same site": CGD-derived
52	# blueprints store far more precision than this, and idealized
53	# coordinates are often exact rationals
54	_SITE_TOL = 1e-4
55	
56	# metric-tensor agreement, relative to the largest entry
57	_METRIC_TOL = 1e-4
58	
59	
60	@dataclass(frozen=True)
61	class SymmetryOperation:
62	    """One space-group operation of a blueprint, in fractional space.
63	
64	    Maps fractional coordinates as ``x -> rotation @ x + translation``
65	    (modulo lattice translations). ``rotation`` is an integer matrix in
66	    the lattice basis; improper operations (det = -1) are included.
67	    ``slot_image[i]`` is the index of the slot that slot ``i`` lands on.
68	    """
69	
70	    rotation: tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]
71	    translation: tuple[float, ...]
72	    slot_image: tuple[int, ...]
73	
74	    @property
75	    def rotation_array(self) -> np.ndarray:
76	        return np.asarray(self.rotation, dtype=float)
77	
78	    @property
79	    def is_proper(self) -> bool:
80	        return bool(np.linalg.det(self.rotation_array) > 0)
81	
82	
83	def _lattice_point_group(matrix: np.ndarray) -> list[np.ndarray]:
84	    """Integer matrices W with W^T G W = G for the cell's metric G.
85	
86	    Entries are searched in {-1, 0, 1}: sufficient for every
87	    conventional crystallographic setting (a centred or badly skewed
88	    cell could in principle need +-2, but no CGD blueprint uses one;
89	    the identity always survives regardless, so the failure mode is
90	    missing operations, never wrong ones).
91	    """
92	    metric = matrix @ matrix.T
93	    scale = float(np.abs(metric).max())
94	    candidates = []
95	    columns = [np.array(c) for c in product((-1, 0, 1), repeat=3) if any(c)]
96	    # build W column by column, pruning on the diagonal of the metric
97	    # condition first (a full 3^9 scan is ~20k matrices; this is
98	    # equivalent but keeps the inner check cheap)
99	    for w in product(columns, repeat=3):
100	        candidate = np.array(w, dtype=int).T
101	        if abs(round(float(np.linalg.det(candidate)))) != 1:
102	            continue
103	        transformed = candidate.T @ metric @ candidate
104	        if np.allclose(transformed, metric, atol=_METRIC_TOL * scale):
105	            candidates.append(candidate)
106	    return candidates
107	
108	
109	def _slot_centers(topology: Topology) -> tuple[np.ndarray, list[int]]:
110	    """Fractional dummy-centroid of every slot, plus its orbit label."""
111	    centers = []
112	    orbits = []
113	    for slot in topology.slots:
114	        dummies = [i for i, site in enumerate(slot.atoms) if site.specie.symbol == "X"]
115	        frac = topology.cell.get_fractional_coords(slot.atoms.cart_coords[dummies])
116	        centers.append(frac.mean(axis=0))
117	        orbit = getattr(slot, "equivalence_class", None)
118	        orbits.append(-1 if orbit is None else int(orbit))
119	    return np.asarray(centers), orbits
120	
121	
122	def _match_sites(
123	    mapped: np.ndarray, centers: np.ndarray, orbits: list[int]
124	) -> list[int] | None:
125	    """Match mapped centres onto the centre set, modulo lattice
126	    translations and preserving orbit labels; None when any site has no
127	    partner or two sites claim the same one."""
128	    image: list[int] = []
129	    used: set[int] = set()
130	    for index, site in enumerate(mapped):
131	        delta = centers - site
132	        delta -= np.round(delta)
133	        distances = np.abs(delta).max(axis=1)
134	        partner = int(np.argmin(distances))
135	        if (
136	            distances[partner] > _SITE_TOL
137	            or partner in used
138	            or orbits[partner] != orbits[index]
139	        ):
140	            return None
141	        used.add(partner)
142	        image.append(partner)
143	    return image
144	
145	
146	def blueprint_operations(topology: Topology) -> list[SymmetryOperation]:
147	    """Space-group operations of a blueprint, from its own embedding.
148	
149	    Every operation maps the slot-centre set onto itself (modulo
150	    lattice translations) with orbit labels preserved, so orbits are
151	    never merged even when two of them happen to be geometrically
152	    superimposable. The identity is always present. For a 2D layer
153	    blueprint the operations are still exact for the stored slab
154	    embedding (c maps to +-c).
155	
156	    Parameters
157	    ----------
158	    topology : Topology
159	        The blueprint; not modified.
160	
161	    Returns
162	    -------
163	    list[SymmetryOperation]
164	        All operations found, identity first. Proper and improper.
165	    """
166	    centers, orbits = _slot_centers(topology)
167	    if not len(centers):
168	        return []
169	    operations: list[SymmetryOperation] = []
170	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
171	    # candidate translations: whatever takes a reference slot (of the
172	    # rarest orbit, to minimize candidates) onto a same-orbit slot
173	    orbit_counts = {orbit: orbits.count(orbit) for orbit in set(orbits)}
174	    reference = min(range(len(centers)), key=lambda i: (orbit_counts[orbits[i]], i))
175	    same_orbit = [i for i, orbit in enumerate(orbits) if orbit == orbits[reference]]
176	    for rotation in _lattice_point_group(topology.cell.matrix):
177	        rotated = centers @ rotation.T
178	        for target in same_orbit:
179	            translation = centers[target] - rotated[reference]
180	            translation -= np.floor(np.round(translation, 6))
181	            image = _match_sites(rotated + translation, centers, orbits)
182	            if image is None:
183	                continue
184	            key = (
185	                tuple(map(tuple, rotation)),
186	                tuple(np.round(translation, 4)),
187	            )
188	            if key in seen:
189	                continue
190	            seen.add(key)
191	            operations.append(
192	                SymmetryOperation(
193	                    rotation=tuple(tuple(int(x) for x in row) for row in rotation),
194	                    translation=tuple(float(x) for x in translation),
195	                    slot_image=tuple(image),
196	                )
197	            )
198	    # identity first, deterministic order after
199	    operations.sort(
200	        key=lambda op: (
201	            op.rotation != ((1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), (0, 0, 1)),
202	            op.rotation,
203	            op.translation,
204	        )
205	    )
206	    return operations

208	
209	@dataclass(frozen=True)
210	class OrbitDisplacements:
211	    """The symmetry-allowed slot displacements of one blueprint.
212	
213	    The free parameters are one fractional displacement per orbit.
214	    ``expand`` turns the packed parameter vector into a per-slot
215	    displacement array with every orbit's members moved consistently.
216	
217	    Attributes
218	    ----------
219	    orbit_of_slot : tuple[int, ...]
220	        Orbit label per slot index.
221	    representatives : dict[int, int]
222	        Orbit label -> representative slot index.
223	    bases : dict[int, np.ndarray]
224	        Orbit label -> (n_free, 3) orthonormal basis (fractional space,
225	        metric-orthonormalized) of the representative's allowed
226	        subspace. An empty (0, 3) basis means the orbit is pinned.
227	    propagation : tuple[np.ndarray, ...]
228	        Per slot: the rotation part taking the representative's
229	        displacement to this slot's, i.e. d_slot = W @ d_rep.
230	    """
231	
232	    orbit_of_slot: tuple[int, ...]
233	    representatives: dict[int, int]
234	    bases: dict[int, np.ndarray]
235	    propagation: tuple[np.ndarray, ...]
236	
237	    @property
238	    def n_free(self) -> int:
239	        """Total free scalar parameters across all orbits."""
240	        return sum(len(basis) for basis in self.bases.values())
241	
242	    def expand(self, free: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
243	        """Per-slot fractional displacements from the packed vector.
244	
245	        Parameters are consumed orbit by orbit in ascending orbit-label
246	        order, ``len(basis)`` scalars each.
247	        """
248	        free = np.asarray(free, dtype=float)
249	        if len(free) != self.n_free:
250	            raise ValueError(
251	                f"Expected {self.n_free} slot parameters, got {len(free)}."
252	            )
253	        rep_displacement: dict[int, np.ndarray] = {}
254	        cursor = 0
255	        for orbit in sorted(self.bases):
256	            basis = self.bases[orbit]
257	            take = len(basis)
258	            rep_displacement[orbit] = (
259	                free[cursor : cursor + take] @ basis if take else np.zeros(3)
260	            )
261	            cursor += take
262	        return np.array(
263	            [
264	                self.propagation[slot] @ rep_displacement[self.orbit_of_slot[slot]]
265	                for slot in range(len(self.orbit_of_slot))
266	            ]
267	        )
268	
269	
270	def _fixed_subspace(rotations: list[np.ndarray], matrix: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
271	    """Orthonormal basis of the common fixed space of the rotations.
272	
273	    Solved in cartesian coordinates (fractional rotation parts are
274	    similar to orthogonal matrices through the cell, and orthonormality
275	    is only meaningful in the metric), then mapped back to fractional.
276	    """
277	    inverse = np.linalg.inv(matrix)
278	    accumulated = np.zeros((0, 3))
279	    for rotation in rotations:
280	        cartesian = matrix.T @ rotation @ inverse.T
281	        accumulated = np.vstack([accumulated, cartesian - np.eye(3)])
282	    if not len(accumulated):
283	        return inverse.copy()  # no constraints: all of R^3
284	    _, singular, vt = np.linalg.svd(accumulated)
285	    rank = int((singular > 1e-6).sum()) if len(singular) else 0
286	    cartesian_basis = vt[rank:] if rank < 3 else np.zeros((0, 3))
287	    # cartesian direction -> fractional displacement
288	    return cartesian_basis @ inverse
289	
290	
291	def orbit_displacements(
292	    topology: Topology, operations: list[SymmetryOperation] | None = None
293	) -> OrbitDisplacements:
294	    """Symmetry-allowed slot-displacement parametrization of a blueprint.
295	
296	    For each orbit, one representative gets the displacement freedom
297	    its site's stabilizer allows (the common fixed space of the
298	    stabilizing rotations); every other member of the orbit moves as
299	    the image of the representative's displacement under one operation
300	    relating them. A blueprint whose every site is fully pinned - pcu,
301	    and high-symmetry nets generally - yields ``n_free == 0``, which is
302	    exactly why those nets build correctly today.
303	
304	    Parameters
305	    ----------
306	    topology : Topology
307	        The blueprint; not modified.
308	    operations : list[SymmetryOperation] or None, optional
309	        Reuse operations from blueprint_operations; computed when
310	        omitted.
311	
312	    Returns
313	    -------
314	    OrbitDisplacements
315	    """
316	    if operations is None:
317	        operations = blueprint_operations(topology)
318	    centers, orbits = _slot_centers(topology)
319	    n_slots = len(centers)
320	    matrix = np.asarray(topology.cell.matrix)
321	    representatives: dict[int, int] = {}
322	    for slot in range(n_slots):
323	        representatives.setdefault(orbits[slot], slot)
324	    # one operation taking the representative onto each member; the
325	    # identity (always present) covers the representative itself
326	    propagation: list[np.ndarray | None] = [None] * n_slots
327	    for orbit, representative in representatives.items():
328	        for operation in operations:
329	            target = operation.slot_image[representative]
330	            if propagation[target] is None and orbits[target] == orbit:
331	                propagation[target] = operation.rotation_array
332	    unreached = [i for i, w in enumerate(propagation) if w is None]
333	    if unreached:
334	        # orbit labels finer than the found symmetry (or operations
335	        # missing): those slots become their own representatives
336	        logger.debug(
337	            f"{len(unreached)} slots not reached from their orbit "
338	            f"representative on {topology.name!r}; freeing them "
339	            "independently."
340	        )
341	        for slot in unreached:
342	            orbits[slot] = max(orbits) + 1
343	            representatives[orbits[slot]] = slot
344	            propagation[slot] = np.eye(3)
345	        # rebuild orbit_of_slot consistency below
346	    bases: dict[int, np.ndarray] = {}
347	    for orbit, representative in representatives.items():
348	        stabilizer = [
349	            operation.rotation_array
350	            for operation in operations
351	            if operation.slot_image[representative] == representative
352	        ]
353	        bases[orbit] = _fixed_subspace(stabilizer, matrix)
354	    return OrbitDisplacements(
355	        orbit_of_slot=tuple(orbits),
356	        representatives=representatives,
357	        bases=bases,
358	        propagation=tuple(w for w in propagation if w is not None),
359	    )

64	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

66	# Constants for cell parameter optimization
67	NELDER_MEAD_XATOL = 0.1  # Absolute tolerance for cell parameter convergence
68	NELDER_MEAD_FATOL = 0.01  # Absolute tolerance for RMSE convergence
69	# Iteration budget PER FREE CELL PARAMETER: cubic optimizes a single
70	# length, triclinic six parameters - a flat budget starved the latter
71	NELDER_MEAD_MAXITER = 100

74	def build_framework(
75	    topology: Topology,
76	    mappings: dict[int, Fragment],
77	    refine_cell: bool = True,
78	    verbose: bool = False,
79	    max_rmsd: float | None = None,
80	    min_distance: float | None = None,
81	    verify_net: bool = False,
82	    relax_embedding: bool = False,
83	) -> Framework:
84	    """Build one framework from validated slot-index mappings.
85	
86	    This is the library-independent core of Autografs.build(): it
87	    needs no SBU or topology library, only a topology and one private
88	    Fragment per slot index, which also makes it usable from worker
89	    processes. Most callers want Autografs.build(), which resolves
90	    names and slot types first.
91	
92	    Parameters
93	    ----------
94	    topology : Topology
95	        The blueprint; not modified.
96	    mappings : dict[int, Fragment]
97	        One (private) Fragment per slot index, as produced by
98	        Autografs._validate_mappings.
99	    refine_cell : bool, optional
100	        Optimize the crystal system's free cell parameters.
101	    verbose : bool, optional
102	        Log alignment details.
103	    max_rmsd : float or None, optional
104	        Directional shape-mismatch gate; see Autografs.build.
105	    min_distance : float or None, optional
106	        Post-build overlap gate; see Autografs.build.
107	    verify_net : bool, optional
108	        Topological gate; see Autografs.build.
109	    relax_embedding : bool, optional
110	        Add the blueprint's slot displacements to the optimization
111	        problem; see Autografs.build.
112	
113	    Returns
114	    -------
115	    Framework
116	        The built framework.
117	    """
118	    t0 = time.time()
119	    plan = autografs.alignment.prepare_build(
120	        topology, mappings, relax_embedding=relax_embedding
121	    )
122	    x0 = plan.initial_parameters()
123	    if refine_cell and plan.has_pairs:
124	        # Nelder-Mead on the packed parameter vector; the objective is
125	        # pure numpy, no object copies per evaluation.
126	        n_free = plan.cell_param.n_free + plan.n_slot_free
127	        result = minimize(
128	            plan.residual,
129	            x0,
130	            method="Nelder-Mead",
131	            options={
132	                "xatol": NELDER_MEAD_XATOL,
133	                "fatol": NELDER_MEAD_FATOL,
134	                "maxiter": NELDER_MEAD_MAXITER * n_free,
135	            },
136	        )
137	        best_parameters = result.x
138	    else:
139	        if verbose:
140	            logger.info("\t[x] No cell refinement performed.")
141	        best_parameters = x0
142	    best_alignment, lattice, slot_rmsds = plan.finalize(best_parameters)
143	    if max_rmsd is not None:
144	        bad_slots = {i: r for i, r in slot_rmsds.items() if r > max_rmsd}
145	        if bad_slots:
146	            worst = max(bad_slots.values())
147	            raise AlignmentError(
148	                f"{len(bad_slots)} of {len(slot_rmsds)} slots exceed "
149	                f"max_rmsd={max_rmsd:.3f} (worst: {worst:.3f}) "
150	                f"on topology {topology.name}: {sorted(bad_slots)}"
151	            )
152	    if verbose:
153	        a, b, c = lattice.abc
154	        alpha, beta, gamma = lattice.angles
155	        logger.info("\t[x] Best cell parameters:")
156	        logger.info(f"\t\ta={a:<.2f} b={b:<.2f} c={c:<.2f}")
157	        logger.info(f"\t\talpha={alpha:<.1f} beta={beta:<.1f} gamma={gamma:<.1f}")
158	        logger.info(
159	            f"\t[x] Aligned {len(best_alignment)} fragments in {time.time() - t0:.1f} seconds"
160	        )
161	    graph = autografs.utils.fragments_to_networkx(
162	        best_alignment, cell=lattice.matrix, slots=sorted(mappings)
163	    )
164	    framework = Framework(graph, name=topology.name)
165	    if min_distance is not None:
166	        contact = framework.min_contact(cutoff=min_distance)
167	        if contact < min_distance:
168	            raise OverlapError(
169	                f"Closest non-bonded contact is {contact:.2f} A, below "
170	                f"min_distance={min_distance:.2f} A, on topology "
171	                f"{topology.name}: overlapping or interpenetrating output."
172	            )
173	    if verify_net:
174	        framework.verify_net(topology)
175	    return framework

178	# combinations are shipped to workers in chunks of this many: the
179	# topology is pickled once per chunk instead of once per combination

183	def _build_one(
184	    topology: Topology,
185	    mappings: dict[int, Fragment],
186	    refine_cell: bool,
187	    max_rmsd: float | None,
188	    min_distance: float | None,
189	) -> Framework | None:
190	    """Worker-safe build: expected failures become None, not raises."""
191	    try:
192	        return build_framework(
193	            topology,
194	            mappings,
195	            refine_cell=refine_cell,
196	            max_rmsd=max_rmsd,
197	            min_distance=min_distance,
198	        )
199	    except (AlignmentError, OverlapError):
200	        # the quality gates rejecting a combination is the expected
201	        # outcome of an enumeration sweep; nothing to report
202	        return None
203	    except (AssertionError, ValueError):
204	        # unexpected failure types: still skip the combination (a sweep
205	        # must not abort), but leave a diagnosable trace instead of
206	        # only inflating the error-rate statistic
207	        logger.debug(f"Unexpected failure building on {topology.name!r}", exc_info=True)
208	        return None

211	def _build_chunk(
212	    args: tuple[Topology, list[dict[int, Fragment]], bool, float | None, float | None],
213	) -> list[Framework | None]:
214	    """Build several combinations against one shared topology pickle."""
215	    topology, chunk, refine_cell, max_rmsd, min_distance = args
216	    return [
217	        _build_one(topology, mappings, refine_cell, max_rmsd, min_distance)
218	        for mappings in chunk
219	    ]

222	def _batched(iterable: Iterable, size: int):
223	    """Consecutive lists of up to ``size`` items (itertools.batched is
224	    3.12+ and the runtime floor is 3.11)."""
225	    iterator = iter(iterable)
226	    while chunk := list(itertools.islice(iterator, size)):
227	        yield chunk

230	def _deduplicate_frameworks(frameworks: list[Framework]) -> list[Framework]:
231	    """Keep the first representative of each equivalence class.
232	
233	    Structures are pre-binned by reduced formula (different formulas
234	    can never match), then compared within a bin with pymatgen's
235	    StructureMatcher at its default tolerances. First occurrence wins,
236	    so the result order is a stable subsequence of the input.
237	    """
238	    from pymatgen.analysis.structure_matcher import StructureMatcher
239	
240	    matcher = StructureMatcher()
241	    kept: list[Framework] = []
242	    kept_by_formula: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
243	    for framework in frameworks:
244	        formula = framework.structure.composition.reduced_formula
245	        indices = kept_by_formula.setdefault(formula, [])
246	        if any(
247	            matcher.fit(kept[index].structure, framework.structure) for index in indices
248	        ):
249	            continue
250	        indices.append(len(kept))

        self,
        topology: Topology,
        mappings: dict[Fragment | int, Fragment | str],
        refine_cell: bool = True,
        verbose: bool = False,
        max_rmsd: float | None = None,
        min_distance: float | None = None,
        verify_net: bool = False,
        relax_embedding: bool = False,
    ) -> Framework:
        """
        Generates a framework from a mapping of SBU to topology slots.

        Parameters
        ----------
        topology : Topology
            the topology to consider
        mappings : dict[Fragment | int, Fragment | str]
            the mappings to go from a slot to a compatible SBU
        refine_cell : bool, optional
            If True, optimizes the cell parameters so that bonded dummy
            pairs coincide, by default True. The analytic starting cell
            is already exact for uninodal isotropic nets.
        verbose : bool, optional
            If True, will log additional information, by default False
        max_rmsd : float or None, optional
            Maximum acceptable per-slot directional RMSD: the shape
            mismatch between the SBU's unit arm vectors and the slot's,
            independent of size (0 = perfect, 2 = opposite). If any
            slot exceeds it, AlignmentError is raised instead of
            silently returning a distorted structure. None (default)
            disables the gate.
        min_distance : float or None, optional
            Minimum acceptable distance in Angstrom between non-bonded
            atoms in the built framework, all periodic images
            included. If any pair is closer, OverlapError is raised
            instead of returning an overlapping or interpenetrating
            structure. None (default) disables the screening.
        verify_net : bool, optional
            If True, verify that the output realizes the requested
            topology by comparing labeled quotient graphs (see
            Framework.verify_net); NetMismatchError is raised on a
            mismatch. Catches mis-paired anchors and wrong periodic
            images, which the geometric gates cannot see. False by
            default.
        relax_embedding : bool, optional
            Embedding relaxation: additionally optimize the slot
            centres as extra optimizer degrees of freedom. Lower-
            symmetry nets can benefit from the extra freedom, while
            fully pinned nets have nothing to relax and build exactly
            as without the flag. The net's declared symmetry is
            preserved by construction. False by default.

        Returns
        -------
        Framework
            The built framework: structure, bond graph, and exports
            (write_cif, to_ase, to_gulp). The underlying networkx
            graph is available as Framework.graph.

        Raises
        ------
        AlignmentError
            If an SBU's connection count does not match its slot, or if
            max_rmsd is set and any slot alignment exceeds it.
        OverlapError
            If min_distance is set and any non-bonded contact in the
            output is closer than it.
        NetMismatchError
            If verify_net is set and the output does not realize the
            blueprint's net.
        ValueError
            If the mappings leave topology slots unfilled.
        """
        validated = self._validate_mappings(topology=topology, mappings=mappings)

            )

            refine_cell=refine_cell,
            verbose=verbose,

        self, topology: Topology, mappings: dict[Fragment | int, Fragment | str]
    ) -> dict[int, Fragment]:
        """Validate and normalize the slot-to-fragment mappings.

        Converts string SBU names to Fragment objects and ensures all
        topology slots have corresponding mappings.

        Parameters
        ----------
        topology : Topology
            The topology blueprint being filled.
        mappings : dict[Fragment | int, Fragment | str]
            User-provided mappings from slot identifiers to SBU names or objects.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[int, Fragment]
            Normalized mappings from slot indices to private Fragment
            copies. Neither the input dict nor the library fragments
            are aliased: alignment mutates fragments in place, and
            shared references would corrupt the SBU library.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If any topology slot is left uncovered by the mappings.
        """

        def to_fragment(value: Fragment | str) -> Fragment:
            return self.sbu[value] if isinstance(value, str) else value

        # slot-type keys first, so that index keys override them
        true_mappings: dict[int, Fragment] = {}
        for k, v in mappings.items():
            if not isinstance(k, int):
                if k not in topology.mappings:
                    valid = ", ".join(repr(s) for s in topology.mappings)
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"{k!r} is not a slot type of topology "
                        f"{topology.name!r}; its slot types are: {valid}. "
                        "Use the keys from list_building_units(sieve=...) "
                        "or plain slot indices."
                    )
                fragment = to_fragment(v)
                for i in topology.mappings[k]:
                    true_mappings[i] = fragment.copy()
        for k, v in mappings.items():
            if isinstance(k, int):
                true_mappings[k] = to_fragment(v).copy()
        all_indices = set(itertools.chain(*topology.mappings.values()))
        missing = all_indices - true_mappings.keys()
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"Unfilled slots in mappings: {sorted(missing)}")
        return true_mappings

# AuToGraFS

[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/AuToGraFS.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/AuToGraFS/)
[![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/AuToGraFS.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/AuToGraFS/)
[![CI](https://github.com/DCoupry/autografs/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/DCoupry/autografs/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/DCoupry/autografs/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/DCoupry/autografs)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/DCoupry/autografs.svg)](https://github.com/DCoupry/autografs/blob/master/LICENSE.txt)

**AuToGraFS** — the *Automatic Topological Generator for Framework Structures* —
generates Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs), Covalent Organic Frameworks (COFs)
and other periodic framework materials by mapping molecular building blocks
(SBUs) onto topological blueprints (nets). It also runs the pipeline in
reverse: deconstruct an experimental structure back into building blocks and
identify its net.

```python
from autografs import Autografs

mofgen = Autografs()
pcu = mofgen.topologies["pcu"]
mof = mofgen.build(pcu, mappings={
    slot: "Zn_mof5_octahedral" if len(slot.atoms.indices_from_symbol("X")) == 6
    else "Benzene_linear"
    for slot in pcu.mappings
})
mof.write_cif("mof5.cif")   # cubic, a = 12.89 A (experiment: 12.9)
```

Original publication: [*"Automatic Topological Generator for Framework
Structures"*](http://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/jp507643v),
Addicoat, Coupry & Heine, *J. Phys. Chem. A* 2014, 118 (40), 9607.

## Why AuToGraFS?

Several excellent framework assemblers exist — notably
[PORMAKE](https://github.com/Sangwon91/PORMAKE) (Lee *et al.*, whose MIT-licensed
building-block library AuToGraFS gratefully bundles) and
[ToBaCCo](https://github.com/tobacco-mofs/tobacco_3.0) (Colón / Gómez-Gualdrón
groups). AuToGraFS was one of the first tools in this space (2014) and version 3
is a ground-up rewrite around a small set of design choices:

- **Works out of the box.** `pip install AuToGraFS` ships **2686 RCSR
  topologies** and **930 building blocks** (63 curated SBUs + the 867-block
  PORMAKE library, 2- to 24-connected). No database generation step, no
  external binaries for building. **96.5 % of the shipped topologies are
  buildable immediately** (see [library coverage](docs/coverage.md)).
- **2D nets are first-class.** The 200 RCSR layer nets (hcb, sql, kgm, ...)
  that COF chemistry builds on are stored as plane-group topologies; a build
  produces a flat layer, and `Framework.stack()` turns it into a bulk crystal
  with AA / AB / serrated / staggered stacking at a chosen interlayer spacing.
- **Geometry, not symmetry tables.** SBUs are matched to slots by optimally
  rotating their connection vectors onto the slot's (Hungarian assignment +
  Kabsch, *proper rotations only* — chiral building blocks are never silently
  mirrored). Point-group labels are metadata, not gates, so low-symmetry (C1)
  vertices stay usable.
- **Physically meaningful cells.** The cell is optimized so that every
  inter-SBU bond sits at its covalent (Cordero) bond length, with the crystal
  system's constraints enforced (a cubic net optimizes a single length).
  MOF-5 comes out cubic at 12.89 Å against the experimental 12.9 — *before*
  any force-field relaxation.

- **Fails loudly, never silently.** Optional hard gates (`max_rmsd`,
  `min_distance`) raise typed exceptions instead of returning distorted or
  interpenetrating structures. Identical inputs give identical outputs.
- **Runs in reverse.** Deconstruct a CIF (MOF or COF) into library-ready SBUs
  and identify its net; harvest a whole SBU library from a folder of
  structures.
- **Rod MOFs, both directions.** The MOF-74 family and other rod MOFs are built
  around an *infinite* 1-periodic metal-oxo chain — no finite building block.
  AuToGraFS deconstructs them, gives each rod a screw-aware canonical identity
  (helicity is chiral and preserved), and **builds them forward again** — for
  straight *and* helical rods, including general (non-180°) screws. See
  [Rod MOFs](docs/rods.md).
- **Post-processing built in.** UFF4MOF assignment on every output, GULP input
  generation, EQeq partial charges, and one-call relaxation — in-process
  LAMMPS/UFF4MOF or any ASE calculator (GFN-FF, GFN1-xTB, DFTB+) — plus elastic
  constants via finite differences (`pip install "autografs[relax]"`).
- **Safe, versioned data formats.** Topology libraries are plain JSON
  (diffable, shareable, survives pymatgen upgrades) — not pickles.
- **A guided CLI.** The `autografs` wizard walks through
  topology → SBUs → build → stack → export without writing a script.
- **MIT licensed**, pure-Python installation on Linux / macOS / Windows.

If you need features AuToGraFS doesn't have yet (see [Roadmap](#roadmap)),
PORMAKE and ToBaCCo are actively maintained and may fit better — comparisons
age quickly, so evaluate against their current versions.

## Installation

```bash
pip install AuToGraFS
```

Requires Python ≥ 3.11. Core dependencies: pymatgen, ASE, numpy, scipy,
networkx.

Optional extras:

```bash
pip install "autografs[relax]"   # UFF4MOF relaxation via LAMMPS
```

On Windows, the LAMMPS wheel additionally needs the Microsoft MPI runtime
(`winget install Microsoft.MSMPI`).

Development install:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/DCoupry/autografs.git
cd autografs
pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

## Quickstart: MOF-5

```python
from autografs import Autografs

mofgen = Autografs()

# what fits the pcu net?
available = mofgen.list_building_units(sieve="pcu")
for slot_type, sbu_names in available.items():
    print(slot_type, len(sbu_names), "candidates")
# Oh 6 : ... candidates      (the octahedral node)
# D*h 2 : ... candidates     (the linear edge)

# pick one SBU per slot type
topology = mofgen.topologies["pcu"]
mappings = {}
for slot_type in topology.mappings:
    n_connections = len(slot_type.atoms.indices_from_symbol("X"))
    if n_connections == 6:
        mappings[slot_type] = "Zn_mof5_octahedral"
    else:
        mappings[slot_type] = "Benzene_linear"

mof = mofgen.build(topology, mappings=mappings)
print(mof)
# Framework('pcu', 'Zn4 H12 C24 O13', abc=(12.89, 12.89, 12.89))

mof.write_cif("mof5.cif")
```

Then keep going: [build options and batch enumeration](docs/building.md),

[deconstruction](docs/deconstruction.md).

## Command line

No script needed — the `autografs` wizard covers build, deconstruct, stack, and
export interactively, and `autografs-topologies` (re)builds a topology library:

```bash
autografs                                    # bundled libraries; guided session
autografs --xyz my_sbus.xyz                  # add custom building blocks
autografs-topologies --use_rcsr -o topologies.json.gz   # regenerate the library
```

Full walkthrough of both commands: [Command line](docs/cli.md).

The README is the overview; the depth lives in `docs/`:

- **[Editing](docs/editing.md)** — editing SBUs before a build, and post-build

- **[Deconstruction](docs/deconstruction.md)** — CIF → SBUs + net, net

- **[Library coverage](docs/coverage.md)** — what fraction of RCSR is buildable

## FAQ

**Does it build COFs?** Yes — 2D layer nets are first-class. Build a flat layer
on a layer net (hcb, sql, ...), then `Framework.stack()` turns it into a bulk
crystal. See [2D COFs and stacking](docs/cofs-and-stacking.md).

**Do I need LAMMPS?** Only for `Framework.relax()`. Building, export,
deconstruction, and everything else are pure-Python. Install the relaxation
backend with `pip install "autografs[relax]"`.

**My SBU is rejected / I get `AlignmentError` — why?** The build gate is
geometric: the SBU's connection-vector *shape* doesn't match the slot's within
`max_rmsd`. Raise `max_rmsd`, pick a net whose vertex figure fits, or edit the
SBU. Point-group symmetry is diagnostic metadata, not the gate.

**Is my net in the library?** 2686 RCSR nets ship; list them with
`mofgen.list_topologies()`. 96.5 % are buildable out of the box — the rest, and
how to enable them, are in [library coverage](docs/coverage.md).

**Does it handle rod MOFs (MOF-74, metal carboxylates)?** Yes — rod MOFs, whose
building unit is an infinite 1-periodic chain, are a first-class case in both
directions: deconstruct them, harvest rod families with a screw-aware canonical
identity, and build them forward (straight *and* helical rods, including general
non-180° screws). See [Rod MOFs](docs/rods.md).

**`deconstruct()` raised `DeconstructionError` — why?** It refuses disordered
structures, molecular crystals (no periodic framework to analyze), *bare*
1-periodic polymers with no framework connections, and 2-periodic (layer)
building units. Rod MOFs and metal-free COFs *are* supported. See
[Deconstruction](docs/deconstruction.md).

**CIF or JSON — which should I save?** CIF for downstream tools, but it loses
the bond graph and per-atom provenance that post-build editing needs. Use
`Framework.save()` / `Framework.load()` (versioned JSON) to keep a framework
editable across sessions.

**Can I still load my old `.pkl` topology library?** Yes, with a warning.
Convert it once with `autografs.topology_io.save_topologies` to the JSON format
and keep that.

## Development

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"

pytest                    # slow tests auto-skipped
pytest -m slow            # only the slow tests
ruff check src tests      # lint
ruff format src tests     # format
mypy src/autografs        # type check
```

Tests live in `tests/`; `scripts/` holds the coverage audit
(`sbu_coverage.py`), the PORMAKE import (`import_pormake_bbs.py`), and fixture
generators. Architecture and module map: [How it works](docs/internals.md).

## Roadmap

The 3.x line has reached feature parity with 2.x and gone well beyond it: the
inverse pipeline (deconstruction, net identification, SBU harvesting for MOFs
and COFs), rod-MOF support in both directions (including helical rods), IZA
zeolite import (`autografs-topologies --use_iza`), partial charges, ASE-driven
relaxation, elastic constants, and commensurate twisted bilayers have all
landed. Remaining directions — cross-linked multi-rod nets (`etb` itself),
EPINET import, and curated high-connectivity SBU packs for the last uncovered
nets — are tracked in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/DCoupry/autografs/issues).

CASES = ["etb-e", "sra", "unc", "pts", "tbo", "sod", "pcu"]

def max_bond_error(framework) -> float:
    graph = framework.graph
    cell = np.asarray(graph.graph["cell"], dtype=float)
    inverse = np.linalg.inv(cell)
    errors = []
    for left, right in graph.edges():
        if graph.nodes[left]["slot"] == graph.nodes[right]["slot"]:
            continue
        delta = np.asarray(graph.nodes[left]["coord"], float) - np.asarray(graph.nodes[right]["coord"], float)
        delta -= np.round(delta @ inverse) @ cell
        target = CovalentRadius.radius[graph.nodes[left]["symbol"]] + CovalentRadius.radius[graph.nodes[right]["symbol"]]
        errors.append(abs(float(np.linalg.norm(delta)) - target))
    return max(errors)

def run(cases=CASES, verbose=True):
    mofgen = Autografs()
    rows = []
    ok = True
    for name in cases:
        topo = mofgen.topologies[name]
        bus = mofgen.list_building_units(sieve=name)
        mappings = {k: v[0] for k, v in bus.items()}
        base = mofgen.build(topo, mappings=dict(mappings), max_rmsd=1.0)
        rel = mofgen.build(topo, mappings=dict(mappings), max_rmsd=1.0, relax_embedding=True)
        be, re_ = max_bond_error(base), max_bond_error(rel)
        bv, rv = float(base.structure.volume), float(rel.structure.volume)
        within = re_ <= be + 0.2
        vol_ok = rv <= 2.0 * bv
        unchanged = (np.allclose(base.structure.lattice.matrix, rel.structure.lattice.matrix)
                     and np.allclose(base.structure.cart_coords, rel.structure.cart_coords))
        if name == "pcu":
            case_ok = unchanged
        else:
            case_ok = within and vol_ok
        ok = ok and case_ok
        rows.append((name, be, re_, bv, rv, within, vol_ok, unchanged, case_ok))
        if verbose:
            print(f"{name:8s} err {be:.4f} -> {re_:.4f} (d={re_-be:+.4f}, {'OK ' if within else 'BAD'}) "
                  f"vol {bv:10.1f} -> {rv:10.1f} (x{rv/bv:.3f}, {'OK ' if vol_ok else 'BAD'}) "
                  f"unchanged={unchanged} => {'PASS' if case_ok else 'FAIL'}")
    print("ALL PASS" if ok else "SOME FAIL")
    return rows

if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    run(args or CASES)
